title: backlog.py check warns of a code item's goal clause that only a file-text check reads
goal: backlog check warns of a goal clause of an item whose touches name code when every check that clause maps to only reads a file's text

run:
import os, sys, json, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(os.path.join(T, 'kb/_self/backlog'))
shutil.copy('backlog.json', T)
item = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', '866e5fdae:kb/_self/backlog/ST-lvcvosht.json'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
d = json.loads(item); d.pop('depends_on', None); d.pop('sprint', None); d['status'] = 'draft'
open(os.path.join(T, 'kb/_self/backlog/ST-lvcvosht.json'), 'w').write(json.dumps(d, indent=2) + '\n')
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/backlog.py', '--root', T, 'check'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
out = p.stdout + p.stderr
hit = [l for l in out.splitlines() if 'ST-lvcvosht' in l and "observer session" in l]
print('warning lines:', hit); sys.exit(0 if hit else 1)

notes: retrospective of SP-ttgcpf7o: ST-lvcvosht's clause "kbask's observer session allows the read-only kb MCP tools" was read only by `'kb_backlog' in open('_tools/kbask.py').read()`; the review found the check weak (no test calls session_argv). The item-level warning that every check only reads files did not fire, since its other check runs backlog.py brief.
